svg.font-family: Inter, Helvetica Neue, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Drill station · spindle control & tool life
svg.desc: Offline ladder drawing for a drilling station, read top to bottom and left to right. Eight numbered and commented rungs: guarded fault reset, three-second spindle speed proving timer, drive-trip or timeout fault latch, edge-triggered start with seal-in and healthy-high stop/safety permissives, a 500-part tool-life counter, a stopped/idle tool-change counter reset, drilling feed permission, and a GEQ comparison that lights an advance tool warning at 450 parts. Allen-Bradley L and U coils, inline ONS and RES brackets, TON EN/DN and CTU CU/DN status terminals. All wires are orthogonal and terminate at the exact contact blade, coil arc, instruction boundary or power rail. Safety STO and drilling motion are handled outside this control routine.
svg.text: Drill station · spindle control & tool life

g.text: Acknowledge spindle fault only with the run command off and the drive healthy.
Allow 3 s to prove spindle speed; also detect sustained loss of speed while running.
Latch a drive trip or speed timeout. Set follows reset, so an active fault wins.
A fresh Start edge seals in the spindle; Stop or loss of any permissive drops the command.
Count each completed part once. CTU detects the rising edge; tool life is 500 parts.
After replacing the tool, reset its count only with the spindle stopped and the cycle idle.
Permit a new drilling cycle only at speed and below the tool-life limit.
Warn at 450 parts so the operator can prepare a tool; the cycle inhibit takes effect at 500.

svg.text: StopOK and SafetyOK = healthy-high. Safety relay operates the drive STO independently.
Timer preset in ms; counter preset in parts. Accum = offline initial value. EN / CU / DN are status terminals.
FeedPermit authorizes the next cycle; clamp, feed motion and safe standstill are handled by the station sequencer.
